items.stem: Which of the following best describes "fossil fuel"?
options: Coal, oil or natural gas formed over millions of years from the remains of living things
The fraction of input energy that is usefully transferred: useful output ÷ total input × 100%
A way energy is held, such as kinetic, gravitational potential, chemical, elastic, thermal or nuclear
Transfer of thermal energy by infrared waves, which can travel through a vacuum
items.answer: Coal, oil or natural gas formed over millions of years from the remains of living things
items.markingKey: A. "fossil fuel" is coal, oil or natural gas formed over millions of years from the remains of living things.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "precipitate"?
options: The total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products in a chemical reaction
An insoluble solid formed when two solutions react
A system where gases can escape or enter
The three things needed for burning: fuel, oxygen and heat
items.answer: An insoluble solid formed when two solutions react
items.markingKey: B. "precipitate" is an insoluble solid formed when two solutions react.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A group of similar cells working together to carry out a function"?
items.answer: tissue
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of tissue.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "An animal that eats producers (a herbivore)"?
items.answer: primary consumer
items.markingKey: B. This is the definition of primary consumer.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "resistance"?
options: The brown wire that carries the alternating pd from the supply
How much a component opposes the current, measured in ohms (Ω)
The rate of energy transfer, measured in watts (W): P = V × I
items.answer: How much a component opposes the current, measured in ohms (Ω)
items.markingKey: C. "resistance" is how much a component opposes the current, measured in ohms (Ω).

items.stem: In an energy level diagram for an exothermic reaction, where are the products?
items.answer: Below the reactants
items.markingKey: A. Energy has been released.

items.stem: A student claims: "The lungs are muscles that pump air." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Lungs have no muscle of their own; the diaphragm and intercostal muscles change chest volume.
items.markingKey: Lungs have no muscle of their own; the diaphragm and intercostal muscles change chest volume. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain the difference between an atom and a molecule.
items.answer: An atom is a single particle of an element; a molecule is two or more atoms chemically bonded together (of the same or different elements).
items.markingKey: An atom is a single particle of an element; a molecule is two or more atoms chemically bonded together (of the same or different elements). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Briefly explain why the mass of a solution equals the mass of solute plus solvent.
items.answer: No particles are lost or created; the solute particles spread out between the solvent particles.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: No particles are lost or created; the solute particles spread out between the solvent particles. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why copper is used for electrical wires.
items.answer: It is a very good electrical conductor and is ductile, so it can be drawn into thin wires.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: It is a very good electrical conductor and is ductile, so it can be drawn into thin wires. (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem:
A class is planning an investigation into how temperature affects the time taken for amylase to digest starch.
(a) Write a focused research question. [1]
(b) Explain how the independent variable will be changed, giving a suitable range. [1]
(c) Describe how the dependent variable will be measured and how many repeats are needed. [2]
(d) Explain how pH (buffer at pH 7) will be controlled and why. [1]
(e) Identify one safety or ethical consideration. [1]
items.answer: (a) How does temperature of the water bath affect time until a sample no longer turns iodine blue-black? (b) temperature of the water bath (°C) – at least five values across a sensible range. (c) time until a sample no longer turns iodine blue-black – tested every 30 s on a spotting tile; at least three repeats and a mean. (d) pH (buffer at pH 7) – pH affects enzyme shape. (e) iodine solution irritates eyes and stains – wear eye protection; take care with hot water baths.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 names IV and DV. (b) 1 method of changing the IV with ≥5 values. (c) 1 measurement method with instrument/units; 1 ≥3 repeats and mean. (d) 1 how and why pH (buffer at pH 7) is controlled (pH affects enzyme shape). (e) 1 relevant point, e.g. iodine solution irritates eyes and stains – wear eye protection; take care with hot water baths.

items.stem:
Leila is investigating how temperature affects the rate of respiration of germinating peas.
(a) State the independent variable. [1]
(b) State the dependent variable and how it will be measured. [1]
(c) Identify two control variables and explain why each must be kept constant. [2]
(d) Formulate a testable hypothesis and explain it using scientific reasoning. [2]
items.answer: (a) temperature of the water bath (°C). (b) distance moved by a coloured liquid drop in a respirometer in 10 minutes. (c) type and age of peas – different seeds respire at different rates; amount of soda lime – it must absorb all the CO₂. (d) If temperature increases up to about 35 °C, then the drop will move further, because enzymes controlling respiration work faster.
items.markingKey: (a) 1: temperature of the water bath (°C). (b) 1: distance moved by a coloured liquid drop in a respirometer in 10 minutes (must include how/units). (c) 1 each, variable + reason: any two of mass of peas (10 g) (more peas respire more); type and age of peas (different seeds respire at different rates); amount of soda lime (it must absorb all the CO₂); time allowed (longer time gives more movement). (d) 1 for a testable if/then prediction linking IV and DV, 1 for correct scientific reasoning: If temperature increases up to about 35 °C, then the drop will move further, because enzymes controlling respiration work faster.

items.stem: Mei plans an investigation into how the vitamin C content of orange juice changes when it is boiled for different times. Describe how the results should be recorded, processed and presented, and explain how the reliability and validity of the conclusion will be judged.
items.answer: Results table with the independent variable (boiling time (0, 5, 10, 15, 20 min)) in the first column and repeat readings of the dependent variable with units in headings; calculate means (ignoring anomalies); plot a suitable graph of the mean dependent variable against the independent variable with a line of best fit; describe the trend and compare with the hypothesis; judge reliability from the spread of repeats and validity from how well variables were controlled.
items.markingKey: 1 table with IV, repeats and units; 1 means calculated, anomalies identified and excluded; 1 appropriate graph (line graph/scatter for continuous IV, bar chart for categorical) with line of best fit; 1 trend compared with hypothesis; 1 reliability (spread of repeats) and validity (controls) discussed.

items.stem:
Diego predicts the outcome of an investigation into how the amount of salt dissolved in water affects its freezing point.
(a) Formulate a hypothesis that includes a scientific explanation. [2]
(b) Identify the independent and dependent variables. [2]
(c) State two variables that must be controlled. [1]
(d) Sketch the shape of the graph you would expect if the hypothesis is correct and explain how it would support the hypothesis. [1]
items.answer: (a) If more salt is dissolved, then the freezing point will be lower, because salt particles get in the way of water particles forming the regular arrangement of ice. (b) IV: mass of salt dissolved in 50 cm³ of water (0, 2, 4, 6, 8 g); DV: freezing point read from the plateau of a cooling curve. (c) stirring with the thermometer; reading interval (30 s). (d) A graph of the DV against the IV showing the predicted trend; if the data follow this trend within the spread of repeats, the hypothesis is supported.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 testable prediction; 1 scientific reasoning: If more salt is dissolved, then the freezing point will be lower, because salt particles get in the way of water particles forming the regular arrangement of ice. (b) 1 IV: mass of salt dissolved in 50 cm³ of water (0, 2, 4, 6, 8 g); 1 DV: freezing point read from the plateau of a cooling curve. (c) 1 any two of volume of water (affects the concentration); the same freezing mixture (ice and salt) (cooling rate affects the curve); stirring with the thermometer (keeps the temperature even); reading interval (30 s) (affects precision of the plateau). (d) 1 graph shape consistent with the hypothesis, linked to support.

items.stem:
Lars counted the number of woodlice under logs at different distances from a stream (three logs at each distance).

Distance from stream / m | Woodlice per log: Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 3
1 | 34 | 33 | 31
3 | 25 | 25 | 26
5 | 12 | 19 | 18
7 | 11 | 11 | 11
9 | 4 | 3 | 4

(a) Identify the anomalous result and suggest one cause. [1]
(b) Calculate the mean woodlice per log for each distance from stream, ignoring the anomaly. [2]
(c) Describe the trend and explain it using scientific reasoning. [2]
(d) State whether the data support the hypothesis that "The number of woodlice decreases as distance from the stream increases." and justify your answer. [1]
items.answer: (a) 12 at 5 m. (b) 1 m: 32.7, 3 m: 25.3, 5 m: 18.5, 7 m: 11.0, 9 m: 3.7. (c) The number of woodlice decreases as distance from the stream increases. Woodlice lose water easily through their exoskeleton, so they live in damp places; soil is damper near the stream. (d) Supported: the means follow the predicted pattern across the range.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 anomaly 12 with a plausible cause (misreading, timing error, uncontrolled variable). (b) M1 method, A1 all means correct: 1 m: 32.7, 3 m: 25.3, 5 m: 18.5, 7 m: 11.0, 9 m: 3.7. (c) 1 trend with data, 1 scientific explanation: Woodlice lose water easily through their exoskeleton, so they live in damp places; soil is damper near the stream. (d) 1 justified conclusion referring to the processed data.

items.stem:
Priya measured the weight of different masses with a newton meter, three times each.

Mass / kg | Weight / N: Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 3
0.1 | 0.83 | 0.86 | 0.86
0.2 | 1.61 | 1.66 | 1.66
0.3 | 2.51 | 2.57 | 2.52
0.4 | 4.67 | 3.33 | 3.46
0.5 | 4.23 | 4.05 | 4.28

(a) Identify the anomalous result and suggest one cause. [1]
(b) Calculate the mean weight for each mass, ignoring the anomaly. [2]
(c) Describe the trend and explain it using scientific reasoning. [2]
(d) State whether the data support the hypothesis that "Weight increases in direct proportion to mass." and justify your answer. [1]
items.answer: (a) 4.67 at 0.4 kg. (b) 0.1 kg: 0.85, 0.2 kg: 1.64, 0.3 kg: 2.53, 0.4 kg: 3.40, 0.5 kg: 4.19. (c) Weight increases in direct proportion to mass. Weight = mass × gravitational field strength; g (about 9.8 N/kg) is constant on Earth, so the graph is a straight line through the origin with gradient g. (d) Supported: the means follow the predicted pattern across the range.

(b) M1 method, A1 all means correct: 0.1 kg: 0.85, 0.2 kg: 1.64, 0.3 kg: 2.53, 0.4 kg: 3.40, 0.5 kg: 4.19 N. (c) 1 trend with data, 1 scientific explanation: Weight = mass × gravitational field strength; g (about 9.8 N/kg) is constant on Earth, so the graph is a straight line through the origin with gradient g. (d) 1 justified conclusion referring to the processed data.

items.stem:
Ingrid counted the number of chloroplasts in cells at different distances below the upper surface of a leaf, three cells at each depth.

items.answer: (a) 18 at 150 µm. (b) 50 µm: 44.7, 100 µm: 35.7, 150 µm: 27.0, 200 µm: 18.0, 250 µm: 9.0. (c) The number of chloroplasts per cell decreases with depth below the upper surface. items.stem:
Aiko used a plug-in energy monitor to measure the energy used by a fan heater running for different times.

Time / h | Energy used / kWh: Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 3

1.0 | 1.32 | 2.10 | 2.11
1.5 | 2.99 | 2.97 | 3.04
2.0 | 4.05 | 4.07 | 4.04

(d) State whether the data support the hypothesis that "The energy used increases in direct proportion to the running time." and justify your answer. [1]
items.answer: (a) 1.32 at 1.0 h. (b) 0.5 h: 1.03, 1.0 h: 2.10, 1.5 h: 3.00, 2.0 h: 4.05, 2.5 h: 5.13. (c) The energy used increases in direct proportion to the running time. items.stem: "Reducing friction is always a good thing." To what extent do you agree with this statement?
items.answer: Friction should be reduced where it wastes energy but kept where it is needed for safety and grip.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: saves energy in machines; reduces wear. Arguments against: friction is needed for walking, brakes, gripping and tyres on roads. Supported judgement: Friction should be reduced where it wastes energy but kept where it is needed for safety and grip. Markbands (15 marks): MYP criterion D (0-8, scaled): 7-8 explains thoroughly how the science is applied to address the issue, discusses and evaluates the implications (moral, ethical, social, economic, political, cultural or environmental), and documents sources consistently; 5-6 explains and discusses; 3-4 outlines; 1-2 states.

items.stem: "Desalination is the best solution to water shortages." To what extent do you agree with this statement?
items.answer: Desalination is valuable in very dry coastal regions but should be combined with saving water and renewable energy.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: unlimited sea water; reliable supply in dry regions. Arguments against: very high energy use and cost; brine harms marine life; saving water and fixing leaks is cheaper. Supported judgement: Desalination is valuable in very dry coastal regions but should be combined with saving water and renewable energy. Markbands (15 marks): MYP criterion D (0-8, scaled): 7-8 explains thoroughly how the science is applied to address the issue, discusses and evaluates the implications (moral, ethical, social, economic, political, cultural or environmental), and documents sources consistently; 5-6 explains and discusses; 3-4 outlines; 1-2 states.

items.markingKey: D. It is lower at high altitude.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "theory"?
options: A version of the experiment without the factor being tested, used for comparison
A relationship where doubling one variable doubles the other; the graph is a straight line through the origin
A well-tested scientific explanation supported by a large body of evidence
A straight line or smooth curve drawn through the data points, with points evenly spread on either side
items.answer: A well-tested scientific explanation supported by a large body of evidence
items.markingKey: C. "theory" is a well-tested scientific explanation supported by a large body of evidence.

items.stem: Explain why excess copper oxide is added to sulfuric acid when making copper sulfate crystals.
items.answer: Excess ensures all the acid is used up; the unreacted solid is then removed by filtration, so the solution contains only the salt.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Excess ensures all the acid is used up; the unreacted solid is then removed by filtration, so the solution contains only the salt. (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Distinguish between its velocity and the speed of a car.
items.answer: Speed is how fast something moves (distance per time); velocity is speed in a given direction.
items.markingKey: Speed is how fast something moves (distance per time); velocity is speed in a given direction. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Distinguish between crystallisation and evaporation to dryness.
items.answer: Evaporation to dryness removes all the solvent quickly, giving small crystals or powder; crystallisation removes some solvent and lets the solution cool slowly, giving larger, purer crystals.
items.markingKey: Evaporation to dryness removes all the solvent quickly, giving small crystals or powder; crystallisation removes some solvent and lets the solution cool slowly, giving larger, purer crystals. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain how fertiliser running off farmland can kill fish in a lake.
items.answer: Algae grow rapidly and block light; plants die; bacteria decompose them and use up oxygen through respiration, so fish suffocate. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Algae grow rapidly and block light; plants die; bacteria decompose them and use up oxygen through respiration, so fish suffocate. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem:
Rafael is investigating how the temperature affects the rate of anaerobic respiration in yeast.
(a) State the independent variable. [1]
(b) State the dependent variable and how it will be measured. [1]
(c) Identify two control variables and explain why each must be kept constant. [2]
(d) Formulate a testable hypothesis and explain it using scientific reasoning. [2]
items.answer: (a) temperature of the water bath (°C). (b) volume of carbon dioxide collected in a gas syringe in 10 minutes. (c) layer of oil on top – keeps oxygen out so respiration is anaerobic; concentration and volume of sugar solution – substrate amount affects the rate. (d) If temperature increases up to about 35 °C, then more CO₂ will be produced, because enzymes in yeast work faster; above 45 °C the rate will fall because enzymes denature.
items.markingKey: (a) 1: temperature of the water bath (°C). (b) 1: volume of carbon dioxide collected in a gas syringe in 10 minutes (must include how/units). (c) 1 each, variable + reason: any two of mass of yeast (more yeast makes more CO₂); concentration and volume of sugar solution (substrate amount affects the rate); layer of oil on top (keeps oxygen out so respiration is anaerobic); time for each reading (longer gives more gas). (d) 1 for a testable if/then prediction linking IV and DV, 1 for correct scientific reasoning: If temperature increases up to about 35 °C, then more CO₂ will be produced, because enzymes in yeast work faster; above 45 °C the rate will fall because enzymes denature.

items.stem:
Sofia is investigating how the concentration of an everyday acid (vinegar) affects the time to dissolve an eggshell piece.
(a) State the independent variable. [1]
(b) State the dependent variable and how it will be measured. [1]
(c) Identify two control variables and explain why each must be kept constant. [2]
(d) Formulate a testable hypothesis and explain it using scientific reasoning. [2]
items.answer: (a) concentration of vinegar (25%, 50%, 75%, 100% diluted with water). (b) time for a 1 cm² eggshell piece to stop fizzing. (c) size of eggshell piece – surface area affects rate; temperature – affects reaction rate. (d) If the vinegar is more concentrated, then the eggshell will dissolve faster, because there are more acid particles to react with the calcium carbonate.
items.markingKey: (a) 1: concentration of vinegar (25%, 50%, 75%, 100% diluted with water). (b) 1: time for a 1 cm² eggshell piece to stop fizzing (must include how/units). (c) 1 each, variable + reason: any two of size of eggshell piece (surface area affects rate); volume of vinegar (20 cm³) (more acid reacts longer); temperature (affects reaction rate); same brand of vinegar (acid content varies). (d) 1 for a testable if/then prediction linking IV and DV, 1 for correct scientific reasoning: If the vinegar is more concentrated, then the eggshell will dissolve faster, because there are more acid particles to react with the calcium carbonate.

items.stem:
Sana recorded the temperature of molten wax as it cooled in a boiling tube (three runs).

Time / min | Temperature / °C: Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 3
0 | 81 | 83 | 82
2 | 69 | 69 | 68
4 | 67 | 69 | 66
6 | 67 | 66 | 88
8 | 55 | 58 | 55

(a) Identify the anomalous result and suggest one cause. [1]
(b) Calculate the mean temperature for each time, ignoring the anomaly. [2]
(c) Describe the trend and explain it using scientific reasoning. [2]
(d) State whether the data support the hypothesis that "The temperature falls quickly for the first 2 minutes, stays almost constant between 2 and 6 minutes (a plateau), then falls again." and justify your answer. [1]
items.answer: (a) 88 at 6 min. (b) 0 min: 82.0, 2 min: 68.7, 4 min: 67.3, 6 min: 66.5, 8 min: 56.0. (c) The temperature falls quickly for the first 2 minutes, stays almost constant between 2 and 6 minutes (a plateau), then falls again. The plateau is where the wax freezes: forces form between particles, releasing energy that keeps the temperature constant. (d) Supported: the means follow the predicted pattern across the range.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 anomaly 88 with a plausible cause (misreading, timing error, uncontrolled variable). (b) M1 method, A1 all means correct: 0 min: 82.0, 2 min: 68.7, 4 min: 67.3, 6 min: 66.5, 8 min: 56.0 °C. (c) 1 trend with data, 1 scientific explanation: The plateau is where the wax freezes: forces form between particles, releasing energy that keeps the temperature constant. items.stem: "The simple particle model (particles as hard spheres) is good enough to explain everything about states of matter." To what extent do you agree with this statement?
items.answer: It is a useful model for many properties but has limits, so scientists use more detailed models when needed.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: explains shape, flow, compression and diffusion. Arguments against: does not show forces between particles or how particles are made of atoms; cannot explain why some substances are harder or have different melting points. Supported judgement: It is a useful model for many properties but has limits, so scientists use more detailed models when needed. Markbands (15 marks): MYP criterion D (0-8, scaled): 7-8 explains thoroughly how the science is applied to address the issue, discusses and evaluates the implications (moral, ethical, social, economic, political, cultural or environmental), and documents sources consistently; 5-6 explains and discusses; 3-4 outlines; 1-2 states.

items.stem: "Rare metals used in phones should be recycled by law." To what extent do you agree with this statement?
items.answer: Recycling laws are justified because supplies are limited and mining causes harm, even if costs are high.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: limited supplies of metals like cobalt and indium; mining damages environments and can involve child labour. Arguments against: recycling small amounts from devices is expensive and complex. Supported judgement: Recycling laws are justified because supplies are limited and mining causes harm, even if costs are high. items.answer: chlorophyll

Unpredictable variation in readings that makes repeats differ; reduced by repeating and averaging
A statement of what the results show, using the data, and whether they support the hypothesis
When an instrument does not read zero when it should, causing a systematic error

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The variety of different species in an area"?
items.answer: biodiversity

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "producer"?
options: A microorganism (bacterium or fungus) that breaks down dead organisms and recycles nutrients
A network of linked food chains in an ecosystem
An organism that makes its own food by photosynthesis, at the start of a food chain
A square frame used to sample plants or slow-moving animals in a known area
items.answer: An organism that makes its own food by photosynthesis, at the start of a food chain
items.markingKey: C. "producer" is an organism that makes its own food by photosynthesis, at the start of a food chain.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "Spread out to the surroundings so that it is less useful"?
items.answer: dissipated
items.markingKey: C. This is the definition of dissipated.

items.stem: Distinguish between an exothermic change such as burning and an endothermic change such as thermal decomposition.
items.answer: An exothermic reaction gives out energy and the temperature rises (e.g. burning); an endothermic reaction takes in energy and the temperature falls (e.g. thermal decomposition).
items.markingKey: An exothermic reaction gives out energy and the temperature rises (e.g. burning); an endothermic reaction takes in energy and the temperature falls (e.g. thermal decomposition). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain why dams are built thicker at the bottom.
items.answer: Water pressure increases with depth, so the bottom of the dam must withstand much greater pressure.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Water pressure increases with depth, so the bottom of the dam must withstand much greater pressure. (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why toothpaste is slightly alkaline.
items.answer: Bacteria in the mouth produce acids from sugar that dissolve tooth enamel; the alkaline toothpaste neutralises them. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Bacteria in the mouth produce acids from sugar that dissolve tooth enamel; the alkaline toothpaste neutralises them. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between amylase and protease.
items.answer: Amylase breaks starch into sugars (mouth, small intestine); protease breaks proteins into amino acids (stomach, small intestine).
items.markingKey: Amylase breaks starch into sugars (mouth, small intestine); protease breaks proteins into amino acids (stomach, small intestine). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem:
Priya predicts the outcome of an investigation into how the number of minutes of exercise affects breathing rate.
(a) Formulate a hypothesis that includes a scientific explanation. [2]
(b) Identify the independent and dependent variables. [2]
(c) State two variables that must be controlled. [1]
(d) Sketch the shape of the graph you would expect if the hypothesis is correct and explain how it would support the hypothesis. [1]
items.answer: (a) If exercise lasts longer, then breathing rate will increase, because muscles respire faster, producing more CO₂ and needing more oxygen. (b) IV: duration of jogging on the spot (0, 1, 2, 3, 4 min); DV: number of breaths per minute counted immediately after exercise. (c) room temperature; the same person. (d) A graph of the DV against the IV showing the predicted trend; if the data follow this trend within the spread of repeats, the hypothesis is supported.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 testable prediction; 1 scientific reasoning: If exercise lasts longer, then breathing rate will increase, because muscles respire faster, producing more CO₂ and needing more oxygen. (b) 1 IV: duration of jogging on the spot (0, 1, 2, 3, 4 min); 1 DV: number of breaths per minute counted immediately after exercise. (c) 1 any two of intensity of jogging (metronome) (faster jogging needs more energy); the same person (fitness differs); rest between trials until breathing is normal (previous exercise affects results); room temperature (heat affects breathing). (d) 1 graph shape consistent with the hypothesis, linked to support.

items.stem:
Arjun is investigating how the type of surface affects the friction force on a sliding block.
(a) State the independent variable. [1]
(b) State the dependent variable and how it will be measured. [1]
(c) Identify two control variables and explain why each must be kept constant. [2]
(d) Formulate a testable hypothesis and explain it using scientific reasoning. [2]
items.answer: (a) surface (wood, carpet, sandpaper, plastic, rubber mat). (b) force on a newton meter needed to pull the block at a steady speed. (c) pulling horizontally at a steady speed – angle and acceleration change the reading; the same block and side – surface of the block affects friction. (d) If the surface is rougher (e.g. sandpaper), then the friction force will be larger, because the surfaces grip and interlock more.
items.markingKey: (a) 1: surface (wood, carpet, sandpaper, plastic, rubber mat). (b) 1: force on a newton meter needed to pull the block at a steady speed (must include how/units). (c) 1 each, variable + reason: any two of mass of the block (heavier blocks have more friction); the same block and side (surface of the block affects friction); pulling horizontally at a steady speed (angle and acceleration change the reading); the same newton meter (meters differ). (d) 1 for a testable if/then prediction linking IV and DV, 1 for correct scientific reasoning: If the surface is rougher (e.g. sandpaper), then the friction force will be larger, because the surfaces grip and interlock more.

items.stem: Yusuf investigated how the length of a constantan wire affects its resistance. The method had this weakness: the wire got warm because the switch was left on. Evaluate how this weakness affects the validity of the results and suggest an improvement to the method.
items.answer: close the switch only while taking readings and use a low current

items.stem:
Yusuf is investigating how the height of a ramp affects the average speed of a toy car travelling down it.
(a) State the independent variable. [1]
(b) State the dependent variable and how it will be measured. [1]
(c) Identify two control variables and explain why each must be kept constant. [2]
(d) Formulate a testable hypothesis and explain it using scientific reasoning. [2]
items.answer: (a) height of the ramp’s raised end (10, 20, 30, 40, 50 cm). (b) average speed = 1.0 m ÷ time measured with light gates. (c) surface of the ramp – friction affects speed; length of the ramp (1.0 m) – distance used in speed calculation. (d) If the ramp is higher, then the car will have a greater average speed, because more gravitational potential energy is converted to kinetic energy.
items.markingKey: (a) 1: height of the ramp’s raised end (10, 20, 30, 40, 50 cm). (b) 1: average speed = 1.0 m ÷ time measured with light gates (must include how/units). (d) 1 for a testable if/then prediction linking IV and DV, 1 for correct scientific reasoning: If the ramp is higher, then the car will have a greater average speed, because more gravitational potential energy is converted to kinetic energy.

items.stem: Design a safe and valid method to investigate how the reactivity of a metal affects the temperature rise when it reacts with hydrochloric acid. In your answer include the variables, the equipment, the range and number of values of the independent variable, the number of repeats, safety and how the data will be recorded and processed.
items.answer: Put 20 cm³ of 1 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid in a polystyrene cup; record temperature; add 0.5 g metal powder and stir; record the highest temperature within 2 minutes; repeat three times for each metal; rank the metals.

Model: Put 20 cm³ of 1 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid in a polystyrene cup; record temperature; add 0.5 g metal powder and stir; record the highest temperature within 2 minutes; repeat three times for each metal; rank the metals.

items.stem: Design a safe and valid method to investigate how the magnification of the objective lens affects the number of cells visible in the field of view. In your answer include the variables, the equipment, the range and number of values of the independent variable, the number of repeats, safety and how the data will be recorded and processed.
items.answer: Place a stained onion slide on the stage; with the ×4 objective, focus and count all whole cells in view; without moving the slide, switch to ×10 and refocus with fine focus, count again; repeat for ×40; move to two other areas and repeat; calculate means.
